issues.description: Mode-selection logic is duplicated in sign_message and verify_signature instead of a single tabulated dispatch.
issues.detail: The four-branch if/elif over SigningMode appears in both sign_message and verify_signature with subtly different default branches. A small lookup table mapping SigningMode -> (preprocessor) would make the invariant explicit and prevent future drift. As written, the reader must compare both functions byte-for-byte to confirm consistency.

issues.description: signing_mode_enum helper has an unreachable-looking fallthrough whose invariant is not stated.
issues.detail: The function enumerates three of four boolean combinations explicitly and falls through to CHIP_0002 for the remaining (not is_hex and safe_mode) case. The reader cannot tell at a glance whether the fallthrough is the intended fourth case or dead defensive code. A truth-table comment or explicit fourth branch would make the invariant literate.

issues.description: verify_signature mixes pure verification with response construction, obscuring the algorithm.
issues.detail: The function computes message_to_verify, runs AugSchemeMPL.verify, then optionally re-derives a puzzle hash and overrides the result. The control flow ends with three return points and a silent override when is_valid is true but address mismatches. Separating message preparation, signature check, and address binding into named steps would make the proof obligations visible.

issues.description: Docstring on verify_signature is a stale stub referencing a nonexistent `request` parameter.
issues.detail: The docstring reads `:param request: :return:` but the signature takes keyword-only signing_mode, public_key, message, signature, address. For a library extracted explicitly to be reused, the literate explanation of what each parameter means and what invariant the function maintains is the whole point.

issues.description: SignMessageResponse dataclass duplicates an existing concept and is not Streamable.
issues.detail: The new SignMessageResponse mirrors fields already present on the RPC response types. Introducing a second near-identical shape forces callers to translate between them. Either reuse the existing response type or document why a separate internal dataclass is needed.

issues.description: New NFT signing test asserts cryptographic equality but never exercises the safe_mode=True hex+CHIP-0002 branch through the RPC verify endpoint.
issues.detail: test_sign_message_by_nft_id reconstructs the expected tree hash inline and calls AugSchemeMPL.verify directly, which proves the signer's math but not that verify_signature (the extracted library function) agrees on the same modes. A round-trip through verify_signature for each of the four modes would close the loop Knuth-style: prove and test.

review.summary: The extraction is directionally correct and removes real duplication across Wallet, DIDWallet, and NFTWallet, but the new signing.py is UNDER-AUDITED as a literate library. The mode-dispatch logic is copy-pasted between sign and verify rather than tabulated, the signing_mode_enum helper has an implicit fourth case, and verify_signature blends preparation, verification, and address-binding into one flow with multiple return points and a stub docstring. Tests prove the signer correct against hand-built expected hashes but do not round-trip through the new verify_signature for all four modes. Verdict: NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT, with one small structural cleanup before this becomes the canonical signing surface for other wallet areas.
